subject: Re: On-demand GPU init latency impacting Fincent scoring
messages:
From: Fincent Ops <ops@fincent.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Cara Lim <cara@fincent.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Init latency impacting scoring — urgent

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sharp regression in p95/p99 for our scoring calls against your Hosted API starting ~14:45 PDT. p95 jumped from ~200ms to ~1.6s and p99 is spiking above 3.5s. This started right after a traffic burst where the autoscaler spun up additional GPU workers.

Impact: batch scoring pipeline is falling behind; downstream retries are piling up. We have an internal SLA window at 16:00 that this will breach.

Can you confirm whether your pool warmup / kernel selection changed in the last deploy? We filed a HubSpot ticket (DEAL-4832) but wanted to raise this in-thread for faster troubleshooting.

Attached: small PNG of our observed SLO series.

Thanks,
Cara
Ops Lead, Fincent
[attachment: fincent_slo_timeseries.png (image/png)]
From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Fincent Ops <ops@fincent.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-06T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Init latency impacting scoring — urgent

Cara —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the chart. We're looking at this now. Initial triage: I see a correlated spike in GPU pool spinups in our telemetry around the same time. Marcus and Neha are on call; Marcus will drop a telemetry dump and a first-pass hypothesis.

Short-term plan:
- Route Fincent traffic to a warm standby pool while we investigate (minutes).
- Disable aggressive burst policy for the affected pool (15–30m).
- If needed, recommend dedicated capacity for their nightly scoring window while we stabilize.

I'll keep you posted in this thread — ETA for standby reroute: ~10m.

Rachel Kim
Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Fincent Engineering <eng@fincent.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T15:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Init latency impacting scoring — urgent

Posting findings from the first 25m of logs/metrics:

- Autoscaler behavior: we saw ~18 new worker boots in the affected pool between 14:40–14:48. Boot durations are bimodal: ~40s (warm cached) and ~220–280s (full init path). The slower boots align with p95/p99 spikes.
- Model variant: several requests were routed to a quantized variant that triggers a different kernel selection path; this path forces larger memory allocations during kernel JIT on some CUDA drivers — likely causing the long init times.
- Node telemetry: a subset of hosts reported intermittent NVML timeouts; OOM events not seen but high memory commit latency observed.

Attachments: heap snapshot (trimmed) and the Fincent SLO timeseries they sent.

Immediate mitigations I pushed:
1) Rerouted Fincent to the warm standby pool (should be effective now).
2) Toggled autoscaler burst to conservative mode for the pool.
3) Blacklisted the quantized variant for the next 30m to avoid JIT churn.

Next: Neha will run the pool warmup script across the remaining hosts and validate kernel cache priming. I will follow up with a postmortem once we have full traces.

[attachment: heap_snapshot-20260906.json (application/json)]
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Fincent Ops <ops@fincent.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Init latency impacting scoring — urgent

Confirming actions and playbook steps executed:

- Warmup: executed the pool warmup across 12 hosts (primed the prefix/KV caches and ran a lightweight synthetic to JIT kernels). Median post-warmup boot time ~38s.
- Telemetry: increased sampling for p95/p99 traces for the affected pool to 100% for the next 45m.
- Fallback policy: ensured request routing will fallback to the warm pool for 30m if init exceeds 120s.

Outstanding: we need to validate driver/kernel mismatch across two host image families (one patched last week). Marcus — can you correlate NV driver version with the slow nodes? If so, we should quarantine that image family from autoscaler until we roll a fix.

Also looping in Evelyn from CS (evelyn_hart@redwood.ai) to surface to our Fincent exec sponsor and coordinate any credit/contract asks.

Neha Kapoor
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Cara Lim <cara@fincent.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Fincent Engineering <eng@fincent.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-06T16:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Init latency impacting scoring — urgent

Appreciate the quick action — routing to warm pool reduced visible p95 to ~220ms in our next window. Two asks from our side:
1) ETA on permanent mitigations / driver quarantine? We run heavy nightly scoring (02:00–05:00 PDT) and a single night with this pattern would cost us materially.
2) Can you provide a short-term option to enable dedicated capacity for those windows while you investigate?

Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Cara
Ops Lead, Fincent
From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Cara Lim <cara@fincent.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-demand GPU init latency impacting Fincent scoring

Cara — quick status and next steps (exec summary for Fincent and internal leadership):

What happened: a subset of hosts running a recently patched driver image triggered long kernel JIT/alloc paths for a quantized model variant. When the autoscaler spun up workers during a traffic surge, those hosts hit long init tails (220–280s), producing the observed p95/p99 regression.

What we did:
- Rerouted Fincent traffic to a warm standby pool within ~10 minutes (restored observed p95 to pre-incident levels).
- Blacklisted the problematic model variant and quarantined the suspect host image family from the autoscaler.
- Ran targeted warmups and primed kernel caches on remaining hosts.

Next steps (timeline):
- Today (within 4h): full driver/kernel correlation report (Marcus) and rollout of an image rollback to the safe family across the fleet.
- 48h: postmortem and remediation plan (root cause, monitoring rule, and automated quarantine).
- Short-term commercial: Aditya will follow up on dedicated capacity offers for Fincent's nightly window and a potential one-off credit.

Meeting: scheduled a quick sync at 12:30 PDT today (invite sent) to review telemetry and agree on capacity/credit.

If Fincent is ok with the dedicated-window option, Aditya — please propose a pricing/commitment outline in the meeting. Evelyn — please prepare a customer-facing summary and the HubSpot update.

Thanks everyone — will post the Marcus report here as soon as available.

Rachel Kim
Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
